scope: The exact64 retained libspdm boundaries in the fixed physical TU117/x86/single-provider/no-CC first-bootstrap profile, including its original error and teardown guards. No cryptographic implementation or GPU runtime verification.

argument: The generated confComputeIsSpdmSupported dispatch selects true only for the listed GH/GB/GR chips; TU117 selects the NV_FALSE method. This is an original chip HAL decision, not an OS readiness flag.

PDB_PROP_SPDM_ENABLED starts NV_FALSE. Its only two NV_TRUE writes in the pinned original RM sources are both guarded by bSpdmSupported obtained from that HAL; a registry request cannot enable SPDM on TU117.

The generic post-load session, pre-unload and destructor paths require the owned Spdm enabled property. The only spdmContextInit call is in spdmEstablishSession, before which these actual entry guards apply. Hopper GSP boot paths are separate HAL routes.
Certificate and attestation controls independently test the support HAL and enabled property; TU117 certificate/attestation/key-update/heartbeat HAL methods also select unsupported defaults.

The common SPDM context constructor checks the real crypto backend before creating the library context. This audit excludes that entry in the fixed profile; it does not relabel a rejected crypto backend as successful.

Cleanup cannot produce a hidden library context: engine construction sets its pointers NULL; deinitialization with a NULL library context goes through a clear helper that does not call libspdm_deinit_context or libspdm_reset_context unless the context pointer is non-NULL.
IS_GSP_CLIENT is runtime device state. It is never treated here as equivalent to the RMCFG_FEATURE_PLATFORM_GSP build macro.

The generated GPU HAL sets PDB_PROP_GPU_CC_FEATURE_CAPABLE false for TU117. The actual global GPU manager is initially zeroed; its first attached GPU copies this property into ccCaps.bHccFeatureCapable, and later GPUs can only AND that capability.

The only two CCSL context allocations in the pinned RM C sources are ccslContextInitViaChannel and ccslContextInitViaKeyId. Both reject the actual global capability before allocating a context or asking libspdm for an AEAD context.

ConfidentialCompute construction initializes all six internal CCSL owners NULL. Encrypt, decrypt and sign reject NULL contexts; clear returns on NULL, and the AEAD free helper requires a non-NULL acquired AEAD owner.

The ordinary GSP RPC queue takes its encryption choice from actual gpuIsCCFeatureEnabled after ConfidentialCompute engine construction; send and receive guard the encryption/decryption calls with that stored queue state. This is a source guard, not an assertion that secure RPC works.

All actual direct calls to generic keystoreDeriveKey in the pinned original RM C sources are inside confComputeDeriveSecrets_GH100. The generated TU117 dispatch selects the unsupported DeriveSecrets method rather than GH100 or GB100.

The direct HKDF/SHA-256 operations in Hopper and Blackwell keystore methods are also behind their exact chip HAL selections. TU117 selects unsupported defaults for these derive/update/seed/init methods.

Generic GSP/Sec2 master-key object creation additionally requires the owned SPDM enabled property, which cannot be obtained in the fixed TU117 profile. No host key object or cryptographic success is fabricated.

One random request is in the NVLE remap-table path, below an encryption-enabled guard and nested loaded/loading GPU loops whose second index starts at the first plus one. The admitted single-provider profile cannot produce that distinct second owned GPU.

The other request is in knvlinkRotateEncryptionKeys_IMPL, whose body has no local CC/NVLE guard. Full pinned C/H token search finds no invocation or address reference except its definition and generated inline wrapper; that search is not a sealed admissible-root proof.

NoCC alone does not prove no NVLE: RMNvLinkEncryption qualification mode can set encryption enabled independently of CC. Checked NvLinkDisable=1 likewise does not by itself prove that a common host NVLink library was never initialized.

The original constructor rejects before applying NVLink overrides if actual nvlink_lib_is_initialized is false. This audit does not invent or establish that backend state; the disabled-library ownership profile must provide it independently.
nvlink-random-partial.remaining_requirement: Seal the actual first-bootstrap, interrupt, error, cancellation and teardown roots against direct or indirect knvlinkRotateEncryptionKeys entry, or implement an appropriate crypto backend. Retain lifetime refusal guards meanwhile.

argument: The original generated dispatch explicitly selects TU102 FWSEC, Booter-load and HS-Falcon methods for TU117. Those firmware paths are required; this audit does not exclude firmware boot or firmware authentication.

Host Booter preparation selects a signed image signature by the actual fuse version and copies its bytes into the image. FWSEC extraction bounds-checks signature metadata and copies signature data; the BIT header check is an explicit byte-sum checksum.

Actual execution prepares Falcon IMEM/DMEM, starts its CPU, waits for halt and checks mailboxes/status. These host functions contain no libspdm/nvspdm references; their signed-firmware execution is distinct from host SPDM X.509 certificate-chain processing.
No signed image, firmware result, or cryptographic verification result is synthesized by these exclusions.
GPU UUID generation calls the separate original nvSha1.h sha1Generate implementation; it does not call a crypto64 libspdm boundary.

Original nvport pseudo-random initialization uses its own seeded xorshift generator and is not a secure-crypto implementation. Conversely, the libspdm get_random_number_64 wrapper calls osGetRandomBytes; that direction does not make ordinary OS entropy requests call libspdm_random_bytes.
This separation prevents treating all hash/random words or firmware signatures as the same unavailable host SPDM operations.

nonlibrary_entry_inventory.scope: All pinned src/nvidia C sources outside libraries/libspdm; comments and strings excluded. This catalogs entry dependencies, not complete indirect-call or operational-root reachability. Linux kernel-open crypto implementations are not supplied by this port.

remaining_requirements: Seal the actual knvlinkRotateEncryptionKeys admissible roots or provide a real crypto backend; neither a lexical no-caller result nor a missing userspace interface closes that requirement.

Preserve lifetime-monotonic crypto refusal counts, both unavailable-symbol mask words and overflow guard. Unexpected invocation must reject apparent adapter success even when an outer status is ignored.
Preserve real firmware Booter/FWSEC authentication and hardware results. Excluding host libspdm certificate processing does not verify a GPU boot.
Original adapter/GSP unwind, bounded waits, stack, ACPI, PM/IRQ and owned-DMA stop gates remain independent requirements.
